clue.text: Pit animal working in extremes of poverty

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outside letters are kept
one thing sitting in another means it goes inside the other's letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of poverty
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A beast toiling down a mine in grinding poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit ponies once hauled coal underground in British mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Small horses were used for hauling coal underground, hence the phrase pit pony for a mine-working horse.

clue.text: Walk in street, then turn round

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for street
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: Someone walks along a street and then turns back.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely, unhurried walk taken for pleasure is described by this noun or verb.

clue.text: Outstanding poem recited?

indicators.note: something recited is spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: an ode is a lyric poem; say it and it matches a word with a different spelling

explanation.surface: Asking whether a remarkable poem was read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the poem, but here it means unpaid, as of a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding bill is one still unpaid, money that remains due to a creditor.

clue.text: Line of latitude runs into field

indicators.note: running into something means going inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
a field of study or discussion is a subject

explanation.surface: A surveyor's line of latitude cuts across a farmer's field.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer and Capricorn are the two parallels named this way, circles marking where the sun is overhead at solstice.

clue.text: Private, secret I broadcast about love

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order
being about something means surrounding it, so the scrambled letters go round another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they have spread a private secret about a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret' looks like a second definition next to 'Private', but it is the letters to be scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small inner circle, so it is restricted and not public.

clue.text: Old capital lifts heart of Dutch queen

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: winches are lifting machines; as a verb, winches means hoists
the centre letter of Dutch
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: An old capital cheers a Dutch queen's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifts heart' reads as cheering up, but 'lifts' is a verb for hoisting and 'heart of' picks a letter. The city was the capital of Wessex and early England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hampshire cathedral city was the royal seat of Alfred the Great's kingdom of Wessex, an early English capital.

clue.text: Fighter beaten up was hot

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are battered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer, beaten up, was left sweating hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reads as part of 'beaten up', but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer, who leads with the right and leaves the left for power, is given this name.

clue.text: Loyalist group kept in touch

indicators.note: something kept in something else is held inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a pat is a light touch
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A loyalist faction stays in contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group kept in touch' sounds like a band staying in contact; it is a three-piece group placed inside a light tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to and ready to defend their country shows national loyalty.

clue.text: Country: one moving with urgency, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what was said points to the spoken form, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: someone who hurries is one who rushes; spoken in a non-rhotic accent it matches a place name

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they heard a nation called a hurried mover.
explanation.walkthrough: The match works in a British accent, where the final r of the hurrying word is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest nation on earth by area, spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia, is this state.

clue.text: Absolutely not where I put sock!

definitions.note: a literal place, read as two plain words

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of scornful disbelief
second meaning: read literally, the part of my body a sock goes on

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark sells the first meaning as indignant protest; the second is the phrase read word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British exclamation of contemptuous denial, and literally names the body part where hosiery is worn.

clue.text: Drop, then fix, mug

blocks.note: a dip is a fall or drop
to stick is to fasten or fix in place

explanation.surface: Instructions: lower a cup, then glue it, then the mug.
explanation.walkthrough: A mug is a gullible fool in British slang, not a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal slang for a stupid or foolish person, just as a mug is a dupe.

clue.text: Cold ice on can sprayed around middle of dirty dish

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre letter, so only that one is kept
something sprayed is scattered in all directions, so the letters land in a new order
going around something means surrounding it, so the rearranged letters wrap another piece

blocks.note: a chill is coldness
the letters to be rearranged
the centre letter of dirty

explanation.surface: Cold ice sprayed on a can around a grimy dish, like a kitchen cleaning mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' sits beside 'ice' as if both were about temperature, but it supplies the first word on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy Tex-Mex stew of minced beef, beans and peppers is a well-known meal.

clue.text: Penny in Angola, the new 50p is like this

definitions.note: describes the coin's shape, so it stands for an adjective

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so these letters are put in a fresh order
one thing in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A penny turns up in Angola, and Britain's new fifty-pence coin looks like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The British 50p (fifty-pence coin) has seven curved sides. 'The new' reads as describing the coin, but 'the' is letters and 'new' signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifty-pence coin has seven sides, and a seven-sided figure is described by this geometric adjective.

clue.text: Patent finished on sixth of inventions

indicators.note: the sixth of a word is its letter in sixth position, so just that one is kept
in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: something finished is over
the sixth letter of inventions

explanation.surface: A patent is granted after an inventor's sixth invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' suggests intellectual property beside 'inventions', but here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain and evident, so something done openly and unconcealed fits.

clue.text: See predicament

blocks.note: first meaning: to notice or catch sight of
second meaning: a tricky situation, as in a tight one

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for noticing something and a noun for an awkward difficult situation, as in being in a tight one.

clue.text: Bully has broken heart: and all fingers and thumbs!

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the letters are put back in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
eight fingers plus two thumbs make ten digits

explanation.surface: A heartbroken bully who is also hopelessly clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All fingers and thumbs' is an idiom for clumsy, but here it is read literally as a count of digits.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, often by warning of harm, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Flower in back of plot, unwanted plant

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of plot
a weed is a plant growing where it is not wanted

explanation.surface: A flower growing at the back of a garden plot turns out to be a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower here is something that flows, a river: the Tweed runs along the border between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is a river, and this one forms part of the Anglo-Scottish border.

clue.text: European city needs empty road developed

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, so only its first and last letters remain
something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written
road with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A city planner says a European city needs its empty road developed.
explanation.definitionFit: This capital of the German state of Saxony, on the Elbe, is famous for its rebuilt baroque centre.

clue.text: Dear: slash price in the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: to slash is to cut
the final letter of price

explanation.surface: A shop sign: expensive, so slash the price eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' and 'price' suggest expensive goods, but dear here means sweet and lovable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear can mean endearing or lovable, and something sweetly attractive is described this way.

clue.text: Comprehensive where castle may have gone?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of a chess move

blocks.note: first meaning: applying to everyone or everything equally
second meaning: a chess castle, or rook, can travel the full width of the chequered playing surface

explanation.walkthrough: A castle is the rook in chess, which moves in straight lines and can sweep the full length of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes changes applying to all categories equally, and literally the path of a rook sweeping the chessboard.

clue.text: Icy edge in sight

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: to spy is to catch sight of
the lip of a cup or cliff is its edge

explanation.surface: An icy ledge comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is informal British for slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy pavement is slick and hard to keep a footing on, which this informal British word describes.

clue.text: Rowing crew steer ahead of bridge

indicators.note: one piece ahead of another comes before it in the order of letters

blocks.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
a ford is a shallow crossing place over a river, a way to bridge it

explanation.surface: A rowing crew steers their boat toward a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like what a cox does, but it is the animal. The Boat Race is an annual rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: The university eight that races Cambridge each spring on the Thames is known by its university's name.

clue.text: Prude finding liar most devious

indicators.note: something devious takes a winding, crooked route, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A prudish person decides that a liar is the most devious of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A prude is someone preoccupied with propriety who preaches and judges the conduct of others.

clue.text: Mark, irritating little thing

blocks.note: first meaning: a check mark showing something is correct
second meaning: a small bloodsucking parasite, also slang for an annoying person

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a checkmark beside a correct item and also a tiny blood-sucking arachnid that bites.

clue.text: Failing, move to the other side

blocks.note: first meaning, as a noun: a flaw or shortcoming
second meaning, as a verb: desert to the opposing camp

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a flaw or imperfection, and a verb for deserting one's country for an enemy.

clue.text: Cook a little quiche, finally

indicators.note: a little of something is just a part of it, so the letters are found within the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A cook finally gets round to making a small quiche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like an end-letter instruction but only supplies letters to the hidden string.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional cook, especially the one in charge of a restaurant kitchen, has this job title.

clue.text: Build higher foundation, for example

blocks.note: to build something is to make it
something higher is further up

explanation.surface: A builder raising the foundations of a house higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Build' and 'foundation' sound like construction, but foundation is the cosmetic base applied to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Foundation is a cosmetic cream applied to the face, one kind of cosmetics in general.

clue.text: Article stopping tooth decay in birds

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, sitting inside the other piece

blocks.note: caries is the dental term for tooth decay
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dentist's report on a filling that stops decay in pet birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' works twice: a dental stopping is a filling, and here it means plugging one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: These small yellow finches, kept as cage songbirds, are a kind of bird.
